about: Version 2's test vectors (CRYPTO.md section 15), made by java/test/avpx/v2/CryptoV2Vectors.java from fixed seeds, and checked on every test run to be exactly what the server's code makes. Bytes are hex. Keys are given as the primitives take them: a P-384 private key as its 48-byte number; an ML-KEM-1024 key pair as FIPS 203's d then z (mlkemSeed, 64 bytes); an encapsulation as its m. handshakeA's steps give h and ck after every step (MixKey steps give the secret mixed and the k made), and its transcript is h after A3 (5.1, point 15). Its datagrams carry a stand-in cookie: a real one is the relay's own HMAC, and only it can check one. result is "valid" or "invalid".

steps.step: start: h = SHA-384(the protocol's name), and ck = h
<- s: MixHash(the relay's static P-384 key)
<- s: MixHash(the relay's static ML-KEM key)
A1, e: MixHash(the game's ephemeral P-384 key)
A1, e: MixHash(the game's ephemeral ML-KEM key)
A1, es: MixKey(ECDH(the game's ephemeral key, the relay's static key))
A1, skem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the relay's static ML-KEM key)
A1: EncryptAndHash(nothing), its tag (k at n = 0)
A2, e: MixHash(the relay's ephemeral P-384 key)
A2, ee: MixKey(ECDH(the relay's ephemeral key, the game's ephemeral key))
A2, ekem: MixHash(the ciphertext to the game's ephemeral ML-KEM key)
A2: EncryptAndHash(the relay's session id) (k at n = 0)
A3: EncryptAndHash(nothing), the game's key confirmation (k at n = 1); h is now the transcript

signatures.scheme: ECDSA P-384 SHA-384, r then s
ECDSA P-384 SHA-384, r then s

refusals.what: a handshake datagram of 1,199 bytes (A1's first, cut short)
a sealed control message of 103 bytes (the game's first, cut short)
a count of 4, for a length that takes 3
a byte after the last fragment's part that isn't 0
the game's first sealed message with a bit of its tag changed
the game's first sealed message with a bit of its message changed
the game's first sealed message again, after it was taken
